claims.text: Every vault on the site is encrypted in the client, so the server never sees a key and the key is the whole question.
claims.quote: the server never sees a key and the key is the whole question

claims.text: The owner's agents now create vaults several a day, and keeping track of the keys has become a real problem.
claims.quote: Now my agents create vaults all the time, several a day, and keeping track of the keys has become a real problem.

claims.text: All vault data is stored in S3 as encrypted objects, served by an SG/Send API server on Lambda behind CloudFront.
claims.quote: All the data is stored in S3 as encrypted objects: commits, trees and files.

claims.text: In the browser the vault key sits after the hash in the URL, which browsers do not send to the server, so decryption happens on the reader's machine.
claims.quote: browsers do not send that part of a URL to the server

claims.text: A vault key is the one secret and carries read and write; a read key and a write key are derived from it one way.
claims.quote: It is the one secret, and it carries read and write.

claims.text: The read key is the site's whole publishing model: read keys are published on purpose and vault keys never are.
claims.quote: The rule is short: read keys yes, on purpose; vault keys never.

claims.text: Append tokens and PKI key pairs are separate credentials that each do one job, so a sender never needs the vault key.
claims.quote: Both exist so that a sender never needs the vault key at all.

claims.text: Vault keys live in two places today: a password manager for keys a person holds, and a registry vault run by its own isolated Claude session.
claims.quote: The registry is a private vault, run by its own Claude session that I keep isolated from everything else

claims.text: The password manager integration does not exist yet, so today a key is copied and pasted into an entry by hand.
claims.quote: The integration does not exist yet (more on that below), so today this is a careful copy and paste into an entry of the right kind.

claims.text: The agent that made a vault seals its key to the registry's public key and sends it with one POST to an append lane, using a write-only token issued to that sender alone.
claims.quote: It sends it with one POST to the registry's append lane, using a write-only token that was issued to that sender alone.

claims.text: A key that disagrees with one the registry already holds is set aside for review and never applied over the old one.
claims.quote: A key that disagrees with one it already holds is set aside for review, never applied over the old one.

claims.text: Two keys in this estate have already been rotated because they were displayed in a chat and the display was captured.
claims.quote: Two keys in this estate have already been rotated for exactly that reason

claims.text: The handover prompt gives the reason before the instruction and gives the agent a way out: seal the key and hand over the file, or hand over the key to be relayed.
claims.quote: It also gives the agent a way out: seal the key and hand me the file, or hand me the key, and I relay it.

claims.text: The sealed handover is safer than what it replaced, a vault key pasted into a chat whose transcript is a durable record held by someone else.
claims.quote: A chat transcript is a durable record held by someone else, for as long as the conversation is kept.

claims.text: The weakest step is getting a key into an agent session safely, because the agent platforms do not have secrets per session.
claims.quote: The hard part is getting the key into the session safely, because the platforms do not have secrets per session.

claims.text: On Claude Code on the web configuration lives on the environment, so the SG/Send access token sits in a variable every session in that environment can read.
claims.quote: configuration lives on the environment, not the session

claims.text: A network secret keeps a server key outside the VM but is per environment and cannot help with a vault key, because decryption happens inside the session.
claims.quote: it cannot help with a vault key at all, because a vault key is not sent to a server

claims.text: Codex's secrets are removed before the agent phase starts, which protects them from the agent and for the same reason cannot give the agent a key to use.
claims.quote: which protects them from the agent and, for the same reason, cannot give the agent a key to use

claims.text: A key for another agent travels in one of three imperfect ways, and the pattern used most is the agent making its own vault and sending the key back on a lane.
claims.quote: which is why that last pattern is the one I use most

claims.text: A lane is a write-only channel attached to a vault: one POST from anywhere, readable only by the vault's owner, with the server keeping only hashes of tokens and keys.
claims.quote: A lane is a write-only channel attached to a vault.

claims.text: Lanes are used for key handover, logging and observation, data from websites, and messages between agents that have no other path.
claims.quote: Messages between agents that have no other path

claims.text: When two or three agents need to work together the owner creates a communication vault just for them, where they use EmailFS and IssuesFS.
claims.quote: If two or three agents need to work together, I create a vault just for them.

claims.text: Small vaults are the right shape for security because a leaked key exposes one conversation, and that is exactly why the number of keys outgrew hand management.
claims.quote: A leaked key exposes one small vault and one conversation, not an inbox, a drive or an account

claims.text: Password manager integrations are the answer wanted for keys people hold; an open call was published and has not yet been followed up.
claims.quote: I have not followed it up yet, so the silence so far is mine, not theirs.

claims.text: secrets.sgit.ai is a secrets manager that runs entirely in the browser and is unlocked by a passkey, whose PRF output derives the wrapping key for the keyring.
claims.quote: a secrets manager that runs entirely in the browser and is unlocked by a passkey

claims.text: One of the WebAuthn spec's editors warns that people lose passkeys and losing the passkey must not mean losing the data.
claims.quote: people lose passkeys, and losing the passkey must not mean losing the data

claims.text: The design has a second root, a 128-bit recovery code shown once, and a wrap per passkey so a second device can unlock the same keyring.
claims.quote: a 128-bit recovery code shown once

claims.text: At v0.1.13 secrets.sgit.ai has shipped the site, the design documents, the mockups and a passkey lab; the app itself is proposed.
claims.quote: the app itself is proposed, and the site is careful to say so

claims.text: The best long-term answer is public and private keys for every party, so a key is shared by sealing it to the recipient's public key.
claims.quote: For me the best long-term answer is public and private keys for every party

claims.text: PKI raises the question of how an agent gets its private key in the first place; the workaround today is a fresh signing key per session pinned by the recipient.
claims.quote: how does an agent get its private key in the first place?

claims.text: Decryption out of band, where you send ciphertext and get plaintext back after proving who you are, is an idea and not yet a design.
claims.quote: That is an idea, not a design yet

claims.text: The owner asks how other people manage their vault keys, or the keys of whatever encrypted system they use with agents.
claims.quote: I would be very interested in how other people manage their vault keys

claims.text: On 10 October the production host still served the older inbox routes while the dev host served the renamed append routes, and the lane address derivation is still proposed at sgit-ai v0.20.0.
claims.quote: It also confirms that the lane address derivation is still proposed at sgit-ai v0.20.0.

claims.text: The article was checked against sgit-ai v0.20.0, the live OpenAPI documents of both API hosts and the site's own pages, all read on 10 October 2026.
claims.quote: Checked against sgit-ai v0.20.0 on this machine

entities.role: the site whose vaults are encrypted in the client and whose docs had the gap
the CLI and vault system whose keys, lanes and PKI are described
S3, Lambda and CloudFront, where the ciphertext is stored and served
the isolated session that runs the registry vault and the sessions that create vaults
the agent platform whose environment variables and network secrets are per environment, not per session
OpenAI's agent platform, whose secrets are removed before the agent phase
the file-based email protocol agents use inside communication vaults
the file-based issues protocol agents use inside communication vaults
the passkey-unlocked browser keyring, one of the four tracks that come next
the passkey standard whose PRF extension derives the keyring's wrapping key
a password manager already unlocking its vault with a PRF-capable passkey
a WebAuthn spec editor who warns that people lose passkeys
the address readers write to with how they manage their own keys

dates.what: The state of vault key management at sgit-ai v0.20.0 and secrets.sgit.ai v0.1.13; the two API hosts' routes checked; the docs updated
